## What this notebook did not do

Where a step needed a package this environment does not ship, the cell said so and continued. An existing message means that step did not run — do not read its absence as a clean result.

Next steps that belong elsewhere:

- **Raw reads to counts** — Cell Ranger and the alignment tools are wrappers, not notebook cells.
- **Differential expression between conditions** — write the pseudobulk tables at the end, then run the `deseq2` wrapper on them.
- **Trajectory, cell-cell communication, spatial, scATAC-seq** — these need packages the plugin environment omits (monocle3, liana, semla, ArchR).

max_counts.comment: maximum UMIs per cell; above this a cell is a likely doublet

mt_max.comment: maximum mitochondrial percent; stressed cells exceed it

n_hvg.comment: number of variable genes to keep

dims.comment: PCs used for neighbours and UMAP

resolution.comment: clustering granularities to try; each gets its own metadata column

seed.comment: random seed, so clustering and embedding repeat exactly

max_genes.comment: upper genes-per-cell bound; null skips the gate

min_counts.comment: lower UMIs-per-cell bound; null skips the gate

quantiles.comment: quantiles reported for each QC metric

detect_doublets.comment: run doublet detection; the script tools default this to false

doublet_expected_rate.comment: expected doublet fraction; null estimates it from cell count

regress_vars.comment: metadata columns to regress out during scaling; use sparingly

group_by.comment: metadata column defining groups for markers/annotation

logfc_threshold.comment: minimum log2 fold change for a marker

min_pct.comment: minimum detection fraction in the group

top_n.comment: top markers printed and written per cluster

max_cells_per_ident.comment: downsample per group for the marker test; null uses all cells

panel_path.comment: marker panel JSON (cell type -> genes); null uses the example panel

mapping_path.comment: explicit cluster -> label JSON; overrides panel scores

min_score.comment: minimum panel score to accept a label

annotation_method.comment: panel or singler (SingleR needs packages this env omits)

group_column.comment: condition column; with it, units are sample x group

min_cells.comment: minimum cells for a pseudobulk unit to be kept

min_samples_per_group.comment: replicates a group needs for a two-group test

min_count.comment: expression filter: counts per unit at least this

min_cells_expressing.comment: expression filter: units expressing a gene at least this many

plot_tag.comment: names the QC plot pass (before/after the filter)

steps.title: Score clusters against a marker panel

4.title: Module 04 — Quality control, clustering, annotation and functional analysis
4.intro:
This notebook runs a Seurat scRNA-seq analysis end to end: quality control,
doublet removal, normalization, clustering, marker genes, cell-type annotation, and
aggregation to pseudobulk for a sample-level comparison.

It picks up where raw-read processing stops. Alignment and Cell Ranger belong to the
wrapper tree; this starts from a count matrix (a Cell Ranger `filtered_feature_bc_matrix`
directory) or a Seurat `.rds`.

Adapted from the scNotebooks curriculum (CC BY 4.0, Rojas-Hidalgo et al., *Nat Genet*,
2026) — https://github.com/integrativebioinformatics/scNotebooks. The explanations follow
the original module; the code is reworked to run in the plugin's private `plugin:seurat` environment (R 4.5 + Seurat 6),
which means no install cells, no Colab paths, and no hidden state between cells.

5.title: Module 05 — Integrating single-cell transcriptomes from multiple samples
5.intro:
Batch effects appear when cells from different donors, protocols, or capture days
are compared: the strongest split in the data reflects the batch, not the biology.

This notebook covers the preprocessing half of the module (normalize through clustering and
embedding) and shows how to judge whether integration helped. Anchor-based integration needs
`SeuratWrappers`/`SeuratData` and Harmony needs `harmony`; both are checked at the point of
use, so the notebook tells you what it cannot do instead of failing halfway.

Adapted from the scNotebooks curriculum (CC BY 4.0).

8.title: Module 08 — Multimodal single-cell analysis (CITE-seq)
8.intro:
CITE-seq measures RNA and surface protein (ADT) in the same cell, so a cluster can be
nailed down by protein evidence rather than inferred from transcripts alone.

This notebook runs the expression analysis, then adds the ADT route: a second assay,
CLR normalization, and a scatter of protein against the RNA for the same gene.

Adapted from the scNotebooks curriculum (CC BY 4.0).

9.title: Module 09 — TCR sequencing and clonotype analysis
9.intro:
Single-cell V(D)J sequencing adds the T-cell receptor sequence to each cell, so
expanded clones can be distinguished from single cells that merely share a state.

This notebook runs the expression analysis on the matching gene-expression matrix and shows
how to join Cell Ranger's contig annotations so clonotype structure can be read against the
clusters. Contig calling itself is Cell Ranger's job, not this notebook's.

Adapted from the scNotebooks curriculum (CC BY 4.0).
